Dearest Traveler,

Chubu is the rooftop of our nation, a mountain fortress dominated by the timeless, snow-capped presence of Mount Fuji. In the cold mornings, the sun rises over the five lakes, painting Fuji’s perfect cone in soft shades of rose and gold. It is a sight that has quieted the minds of poets and travelers for millennia.

Deep within the mountain creases, the steep-roofed wooden houses of Shirakawa-go look like hands folded in prayer, built to survive winters of incredible snow. Along the old Nakasendo path, the post towns of Tsumago and Magome preserve the cobblestones walked by samurai. Chubu teaches us the nobility of endurance, and the peace of looking upward.

With towering peace,
Kokoro of Chubu
